Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 20-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  AI in Cyber Security [IT_4004]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Using a suitable example, explain how supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms can               (5)  
  be applied in cybersecurity for anomaly detection and threat classification. Illustrate the process  
  A)           with a labeled diagram or workflow.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Design a use case scenario where machine learning techniques enhance cybersecurity-such as (5)  
  spam filtering, intrusion detection, or ransomware detection. Outline the dataset features, model  
  type, and expected outcomes.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                                                                                                                        (5)  
  
  
  A)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  Page #1

B)               Compare and contrast signature-based and behavior-based malware detection approaches.            (5)  
  Analyze which method is more effective in detecting zero-day malware and justify your reasoning.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                       Analyze the impact of feature selection and dimensionality reduction (e.g., using PCA) on the         (5)  
  accuracy and interpretability of ML models used in cyber threat detection. Provide a suitable  
  A)               justification with examples.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)               Discuss how deep neural networks (DNNs) improve accuracy and adaptability in intrusion detection (5)  
  systems (IDS). Illustrate with an example from recent cyberattack scenarios.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)                       Examine a case study on detecting DDoS or brute-force attacks using LSTM or CNN models.               (5)  
  Discuss model design, dataset used, and results obtained.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)               Compare the performance and characteristics of traditional machine learning (e.g., SVM, KNN) and (5)  
  deep learning models (e.g., CNN, LSTM) for intrusion detection. Analyze which approach is more  
  effective for large-scale, high-dimensional network datasets.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)                       Discuss how GAN-based adversarial attacks exploit the interaction between the generator and           (5)  
  discriminator networks. Analyze why GAN-based attacks are considered a major threat to image  
  A)               classification and deepfake generation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)               Explain how an adversary can manipulate training data to perform a poisoning attack. Differentiate    (5)  
  between dataset poisoning, algorithm poisoning, and model poisoning with suitable cybersecurity  
  examples.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
